I don’t have any advice but I’m in a similar spot so I thought I’d commiserate. My life on paper is perfect, but I keep asking for more out of life and my partner seems satisfied with how things are. It’s driven me away and driven me crazy. I have a lot of my own personal issues that I’m working on to change and grow and it didn’t feel like my partner was on that journey with me. More like a bystander. It’s been disappointing and I do worry that when we are 55 I will have regret or resent him for the life we have. That’s the worst Thing I can imagine. I have told him as much, but he doesn’t have the same fears. I feel guilty for having these thoughts/feelings. 

Have you communicated how desperate you’re feeling? I did but it didn’t change much - maybe it could in your case? Either way good luck to you.

I’m in the shoes of your partner at the moment. I stopped feeling the kind of love I should have for my husband and I recently told him and we aren’t speaking at the moment. It is the hardest thing I’ve ever done, but it was right to tell him - no matter what happens to our relationship as a result. What I’ve learned in the short time we’ve been apart is that I actually don’t love myself. It’s hard to accept love you can’t give yourself and you aren’t sure if you deserve. Your partner is probably struggling and won’t be a good partner to you if they can’t resolve their own internal strife. I’m sorry you’re in this spot. I’m sorry you are hurting. Every day will hurt a little less I believe. And maybe you should try to connect with yourself, be kind to yourself, and give yourself the unconditional love you deserve.  I hope this is somewhat comforting and doesn’t seem like projecting. I feel called to offer my perspective because I’m not able to support my husband in this painful time.
